newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeri voucher auctions put off until mid-May.
newsitem.headline: Azeri voucher auctions put off until mid-May.

text.p: Azerbaijan has put off the beginning of auctions to sell off most of state-held assets until at least mid-May, because of delays in distributing privatisation vouchers, a State Property Committee official said on Wednesday.
"This is due to the slow pace of distribution of privatisation vouchers to the population," said Adalyat Teimurov, an official at the committee, which is Azerbaijan's privatisation ministry.
As in many East European countries, the Azeri government is providing its citizens with vouchers which can be used to bid for shares in companies being privatised.
Only 45 percent of Azeris had received the four-voucher booklets in the first six weeks of distribution, Teimurov said.
The government wanted at least 50 percent of residents to have received them by the time the auctions begin, he said.
"In May, when more than half of the population has received them, it will be possible to begin auctions," he said.
Auctions to privatise 59 medium-sized state enterprises were originally to have begun in late March. That date was later pushed back to mid-April.

The voucher booklets have seen their value plummet in recent weeks to a record low 90,000 manats ($22.50) in street trading. Their highest value was about 450,000 manats ($120) in mid-March, two weeks after being introduced.
The booklets have no nominal value, but State Property Committee officials have estimated their real worth at about $800.
This assumes the total value of all state property to be auctioned off is 49 trillion manats ($12 billion). Eight million of the booklets have been printed, one for each of Azerbaijan's citizens.
Seventy percent of state-owned enterprises will be sold off but 30 percent, including the vital oil sector, will stay in government hands.
